subject: Request: transient SLA carveout for Argent alpha model rollout
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Carolyn Santos <carolyn@nimblehealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Argent alpha - transient SLA carveout request

Hi Carolyn —

Thanks again for the time on Thursday. NimbleHealth's integration with Argent is shaping up well; appreciate the early feedback from your team.

Quick ask from our side: Argent is still an alpha/preview model (internal codename: Argent-alpha). For the initial staged rollout we want to put an explicit operational carveout in place so both sides have a clear expectation while we complete performance tuning. The proposal in the attached "argent-alpha-slo-proposal.pdf" is to treat the alpha deployment as a transient preview for 30 days with the following temporary SLOs (applied only to traffic explicitly routed to the Argent-alpha variant):

- Availability: 95% (30-day window) vs our standard 99.9%
- Latency: p95 <= 200ms for generation endpoints (stable models remain at current p95 targets)
- Error budget: expanded to accommodate model warmup / kv-cache misses during alpha tasks

In return we will:
- Run a 10% canary of real user traffic for 30 days with auto-fallback to your stable model on any degradation
- Provide daily health/slo dashboards and a live slack channel for alerts
- Commit to an engineering cadence to hit standard SLOs (99.9 / 150ms p95) within the 30-day window or propose a narrow extension with justification

Can you confirm whether NimbleHealth is open to a temporary carveout along these lines? If so we can loop in legal for a short amendment and schedule an exec sign-off. Attaching a canary rollout plan as well.

Thanks —
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Account Lead, Strategic Partners
Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: argent-alpha-slo-proposal.pdf, canary-rollout-plan.xlsx

From: Carolyn Santos <carolyn@nimblehealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@nimblehealth.com>, NimbleHealth Legal <legal@nimblehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Argent alpha - transient SLA carveout request

Hannah —

Appreciate the clear proposal and the attachments. High level NimbleHealth position: we are comfortable with a preview carveout in principle, provided we have:

1) A firm, timeboxed scope (we prefer 30 days but need to see the rollback conditions)
2) A clear fallback (auto-routing to our existing stable model) and visibility into errors/latency
3) Commercial protections: either a small service credit if Argent-alpha causes >5 incidents impacting >1% of our traffic, or a temporary discounted rate for preview traffic

Legal will want to see the exact amendment language. I copied Tom (ops) and Legal. Please send the canary signal thresholds and rollback triggers you mentioned so we can review with our SREs.

One other ask from our side: we need confirmation that PII/PHI handling for preview traffic is identical to production handling (no different retention or logging). If any telemetry is collected for tuning we need it flagged and agreed.

Thanks —
Carolyn
Carolyn Santos
Head of Integrations
NimbleHealth
carolyn@nimblehealth.com

Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 15:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Argent alpha - transient SLA carveout request (technical safeguards)

Hannah / team —

Quick technical note to address Nimble's asks:

- Canary signal thresholds: we recommend immediate rollback if (1) error rate >1.5x baseline for >10 minutes, (2) latency p95 > 300ms for >15 minutes, or (3) any user-facing correctness regression flagged by their QA set. Those are included in the canary workbook.
- Auto-fallback: we can enforce weighted routing with instant fallback to stable-argent-v1 (0s TTL on fallback rule) so no customer requests are routed to alpha during an incident window. Failover testing is scheduled for Jun 26.
- Telemetry / data handling: preview traffic will be logged identical to production; no separate retention or replication. Any model-specific telemetry used for tuning will be redacted of PII and stored behind the same KMS keys. Security team confirmed via a short call with Nimble that there are no additional exposures.
- Mitigations for latency: enabling reduced KV prefetch (saves ~30ms p95) and a conservative quantization profile for alpha. That reduces expected p95 from ~260ms to ~190–210ms depending on prompt length.

If legal needs a short addendum, we can propose a 1-page amendment that:
1) timeboxes the carveout to 30 days (with one 14-day extension by mutual agreement),
2) lists the fallback rules and rollback triggers, and
3) defines the commercial credit trigger (e.g., 5 incidents -> 5% credit on preview usage).

I recommend we confirm the 30-day window to Nimble and simultaneously circulate a draft amendment to Legal.

—Dev

Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 16:08:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Argent alpha - transient SLA carveout request

Carolyn / Tom —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and for surfacing the legal/commercial asks. Per Dev's note and after a brief leadership review with Marissa and Karthik, Redwood can agree to the transient carveout with the following negotiated items:

- Carveout window: 30 days from first production canary traffic (start date to be agreed; target July 6) with one 14-day extension by mutual written agreement.
- Target SLOs for alpha traffic: 95% availability, p95 latency <= 200ms.
- Canary: 10% traffic initially; rollback triggers are as Dev specified. Auto-fallback to stable-argent-v1 is enabled and will be tested prior to start.
- Commercial protection: Redwood will provide a single 5% service credit on preview usage if Argent-alpha causes >=5 incidents that affect >1% of NimbleHealth traffic during the carveout window.
- Data handling: No changes to PII/PHI retention. Any telemetry used for model tuning will be redacted and stored under Nimble's same KMS.

Next steps:
1) If Nimble agrees, legal teams can sign a 1-page amendment. I've attached a marked-up term sheet (legal-term-markup-20260628.pdf) for quick review.
2) Dev will execute a failover test with Tom on Jul 2.
3) We’ll send a DocuSign link for the amendment and schedule the first-weekly health check channel.

Carolyn — can you confirm acceptance of the above (timebox/credit/fallback/data) and whether you prefer the credit or a discounted preview rate? Once we have that I’ll ping Legal to route the DocuSign.

—Hannah
